 WHO Urges Clearing Stagnant Water to Prevent Dengue Fever Spread 
 November 7, 2026 1 minute read 
 The World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Saturday, November 6th, that mosquitoes carrying dengue fever lay eggs in stagnant water containers inside and outside homes, leading to the spread of the disease. The agency urged the public to cover water tanks and empty and clean water storage containers weekly. It also recommended regularly changing the water in flowerpots.
 WHO supported the disposal of plastic items such as bottles, tires, and cans that collect water, emphasizing that even bottle caps can serve as suitable breeding grounds for mosquitoes. Keeping ditches and drains clean was also introduced as an effective way to reduce mosquito presence.
 This warning comes after the same agency reported an increase in dengue fever cases in eastern Afghanistan on Thursday. This development represents a serious public health concern in the affected areas and underscores the urgent need for decisive measures to control the disease.
